subject: Egress connector design & IP allowlisting for Aurora Health private deployment
messages:
From: Amelia Park <amelia.park@aurora-health.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: NetWave Solutions <netsales@netwave.io>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:17 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment networking — initial egress ask

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the quick intro call today. We're excited to move forward with the Private deployment for our clinical inference workloads. Before we lock an install window our security team needs a concrete list of outbound endpoints and a recommended firewall policy for the private endpoint nodes (control plane + runtime).

High-level asks from Aurora security:
- A definitive set of IP ranges (or FQDNs) that must be allowed outbound from the VPC/on-prem environment to Redwood control plane and telemetry endpoints
- Ports and protocols (TCP/UDP) required, and whether TLS is mandatory on each path
- Guidance for DNS resolution (do you require split-horizon or can FQDN allowlisting suffice?)
- Audit/logging guidance and any expectations for mTLS or client certs
- Plan for IP rotation or failover (we cannot accept frequent surprises during maintenance windows)

Can you provide a recommended policy draft (we can share with our firewall admins) plus any diagrams? NetWave is on the thread to help with the edge/proxy questions.

Appreciate it — we'd like to get this into our change window the week of May 24.

Best,
Amelia Park
Senior PM, Cloud Integrations
Aurora Health

[Attachment: aurora-soc2-questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Park <amelia.park@aurora-health.com>
Cc: NetWave Solutions <netsales@netwave.io>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:08:52 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment networking — initial egress ask

Amelia —

Thanks for the clear list. I attached a concise proposal (egress-ip-range-proposal.csv) and a simple diagram (networking-diagram-v1.png) to start — both are drafts and we can finalize after the tech review. High-level responses:

- We provide a small set of stable public egress IPs for control-plane callbacks (primary + standby) that you can allow at the perimeter. The CSV contains the current CIDR blocks and a human-readable mapping.
- All control-plane and telemetry traffic MUST be TLS 1.2+ (we recommend 1.3) over TCP 443. No UDP required.
- For runtime model traffic (inference upload / KV cache sync) we recommend FQDN allowlisting for the runtime-specific buckets; these resolve to the same egress IPs but we recognize some orgs prefer names. We support both models.
- DNS: FQDN allowlisting is acceptable for most customers, but if you have strict egress proxies that only work with IP-level allowlists, use the IP list. We document implications for CDN-backed endpoints in the CSV.
- Rotation: Redwood commits to a 30-day notice for any planned changes to the published IP list; emergency rotations will be communicated via the dedicated slack channel + support escalation path.
- Audit: we emit per-request traces and recommend shipping flow logs from your perimeter to your SIEM. We can provide a sample mapping of Redwood trace IDs to request metadata.

Next step: Rafael will follow up with specific port numbers and some implementation options (NAT gateway static IPs vs. on-prem egress proxies with mTLS). Could NetWave propose proxy integration notes once they've had a look?

Proposed meeting: Tech review Wednesday May 19, 11:00am PT — can you and NetWave make that?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: egress-ip-range-proposal.csv (text/csv), networking-diagram-v1.png (image/png)]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Park <amelia.park@aurora-health.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 15:23:04 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment networking — initial egress ask

Amelia / team —

Quick technical note ahead of the call:

1) Ports/protocols
- 443/TCP: control-plane callbacks, heartbeat, telemetry ingestion (TLS mandatory)
- 5222/TCP: optional internal agent heartbeat for older on-prem installs (we avoid this for new customers; will not be required)
- 8443/TCP: internal admin endpoints (only allow from your admin subnet and our customer VPN endpoints)

2) NAT vs proxy patterns
- If you want a single static egress IP, route runtime/control traffic through a NAT gateway (cloud) or a dedicated egress proxy appliance (on-prem).
- If you rely on corporate outbound proxies, we support outbound proxy chaining. In that case Redwood's control callbacks will originate from the proxy IPs; you must ensure the proxy allows CONNECT to our target FQDNs and preserves SNI.

3) DNS considerations
- SNI-aware firewalls: if your perimeter filters on SNI we strongly recommend FQDN/SNI allowlisting because our IPs are fronted by a CDN. Blocking by IP only can cause intermittent failures during upstream changes.

4) mTLS / client certs
- For management/control endpoints we offer mutual TLS as an opt-in for customers who need stronger identity guarantees. If Aurora requests mTLS we will share certificate fingerprints and rotation cadence.

5) Failover & maintenance
- We publish a primary and standby egress set. During maintenance we fail over to standby; we will post banner notices to your console and email a 72-hour change notice for planned rotations.

I'll attach a short explainer (redwood-controlplane-callbacks.md) that maps each callback to an intended port and FQDN — this should help the firewall team.

—Rafael
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood-controlplane-callbacks.md (text/markdown)]

From: NetWave Solutions <netsales@netwave.io>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Amelia Park <amelia.park@aurora-health.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:45:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment networking — initial egress ask

Hi all —

NetWave here. Quick notes from the edge/proxy side after reviewing the diagram:
- Aurora's perimeter sits behind a corporate outbound proxy that performs TLS interception. That means SNI is rewritten in some paths and the proxy performs connection re-termination. Allowlisting by IP is simpler for us but Aurora’s security team prefers hostname-level controls where possible.
- If Redwood can present a short, stable hostname list and commit to the 30-day notice for changes, we can map stable DNS entries to fixed egress translation rules in our proxy (reduces operational churn).
- Audit/logging: we'll need per-connection metadata forwarded to Aurora's SIEM (session ID, source node, upstream SNI, egress IP chosen). Please confirm Redwood's trace ID surface area so we can correlate.
- Edge TLS cert pinning: we can support mTLS to Redwood if you provide CA bundle and a rotation schedule.

We'll join the May 19 tech call to walk the proxy options.

—Priya (on behalf of NetWave)
Solutions Architect
NetWave Solutions

- NetWave will prepare proxy translation rules for the hostnames we publish; Aurora to confirm whether proxy will preserve SNI for CONNECT flows.
- Redwood will provide a sample flow-log mapping file so Aurora can correlate SF logs with our request traces.
